chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Zurara, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) and Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who lends another man silver (dirhams) on the condition that he repays it to him in another land, and stipulates that for him, he said: 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: there is no objection/it is permissible
key_terms.يُسْلِفُ: lends money or goods as a loan

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to stipulate repayment in a different location when lending money in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted through the reliable chain of Zurara and Safwan, clarifies the permissibility of stipulating a specific location for the repayment of a silver debt (qard al-waraq), distinguishing it from interest-based conditions. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that geographical stipulations in loans are valid contractual terms rather than defects, ensuring clarity in financial transactions. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Islamic commercial law to accommodate practical needs while maintaining the integrity of the loan contract.
